query: Which material can be used for ductility, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Copper exhibits enhanced ductility when subjected to annealing processes.
generation.conditions: Controlled atmosphere to prevent oxidation during annealing.
generation.structural_mediator: Grain growth and recovery mechanisms in the copper microstructure.
generation.mechanism: Annealing allows dislocations to rearrange and reduce internal stresses, leading to increased ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: The ductility of copper will increase significantly after annealing compared to its cold-worked state.
generation.baseline: Cold-worked copper with known lower ductility.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies specifically to copper and similar ductile metals undergoing annealing.
generation.uncertainty: The exact temperature and duration of annealing required for optimal ductility improvement are not specified.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a series of tensile tests on cold-worked copper samples before and after annealing at various temperatures and durations.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ductility (elongation percentage) of the annealed samples does not exceed that of the cold-worked samples, the hypothesis is falsified.
